paper.title_en: Unstable Periodic Orbit Localization in a Nonlinear System-Environment Model
paper.abstract_en: The role of unstable periodic orbits (UPOs) is investigated in the chaotic dynamics of a nonlinear system-environment model composed of a central two-level system coupled to an environment of two-level systems. Families of UPOs embedded in chaotic regions are identified and their local instability is characterized. Their behavior is examined under variations of the environment size, energy, and system symmetry, allowing the model to serve as a controlled testbed in which the dimensionality and dynamical conditions can be systematically modified. Characteristic UPO-based dynamical quantities are used to assess the influence of these periodic orbits on nearby chaotic trajectories, including occupation of the UPO tube, its persistence at late times, return fidelity enhancement, and recurrence timing. Across the different model variations considered, trajectories initialized close to the UPOs retain statistically detectable spatial and temporal signatures associated with the periodic orbits. These results indicate that unstable periodic orbits can retain a measurable organizing influence on surrounding chaotic trajectories across changes in dimensionality, energy, and system symmetry, giving rise to scar-like dynamical signatures in a simple nonlinear system--environment model.
